messages:
maria: Heads-up — we saw sustained GPU pool utilization >95% in eu-west-1 for ~18m during the morning traffic spike. Several user routes started seeing 503s.
devin: saw it too. queue length on the frontend jumped, then admission started rejecting 10% of requests. p95 latency for routed requests spiked from 180ms -> 1.6s.
linh: Did autoscaler attempt to spin more nodes? I saw no new pods in the cluster during the window.
ops-bot: autoscaler-event: scale up attempted but rate-limited by region quota (gpus), request queued.
samir: Region quota is the root cause for the scale failure. We can't immediately add capacity in eu-west. Need short-term policy change so customer-facing routes degrade instead of hard-rejecting.
azeem: I propose a three-tier policy: 1) soft-queue with max TTL 6s, 2) graceful-degrade for interactive routes (reduce max_tokens or compress output), 3) reject for bulk/rerank background jobs. Thoughts?
maria: +1 conceptually. We need a clear signal from the scheduler to the edge so the API gateway can decide: queue vs degrade vs reject.
devin: Implementation detail: scheduler can emit a saturation signal with fields: pool_util, estimated_wait_ms, allowed_mode [queue|degrade|reject]. API gateway then uses route policy to act.
linh: For degrade mode, what exact degradation? Trimming replies? switching to smaller model? returning partial stream?
samir: Prefer model fallback + token cap first, then trimming. Fallback to a 3B quantized variant preserves semantics better than trimming random tokens.
azeem: Also a cheap fast-fail check: if request is non-interactive (header x-retryable: true) and queue > N, reject immediately and return Retry-After.
maria: Need telemetry: track how many times we apply degrade vs reject, user-visible errors, and quality regressions. Hook into Redwood Console evals.
devin: Rough config sketch:
```
admission_policy:
  saturation_threshold: 0.92
  modes:
    - name: soft_queue
      ttl_ms: 6000
      max_wait: 200
    - name: degrade
      actions: [model_fallback, token_cap(512), compress_response]
    - name: reject
      status: 503
```
linh: Concern: soft_queue can increase tail latency because requests sit in the gateway. We should prefer pre-queueing at router level with backpressure to clients and instrumentation for queue depth.
samir: Agree. Make soft_queue opt-in per-route. Interactive chat routes get it, batch endpoints do not.
azeem: Cost note: degrade -> smaller model use reduces spend per token by ~10-20% but increases error window. We need rollback metrics.
maria: Action items: (1) devin/linh implement saturation signal proto + gateway hook. (2) samir prepare degrade fallback runbook and model variants mapping. (3) azeem add dashboards and alerts for degrade/reject counts and quality regression signals. (4) ops to request temporary quota bump for eu-west.
devin: I can start a prototype PR for the signal and gateway behavior today. Will add a lightweight header x-sat-mode.
linh: I'll mock the gateway logic and test with locust against a local gpu pool simulator.
samir: I'll draft the runbook and notify support + status page templates.
maria: Thanks. Let's keep the soft-queue TTL conservative; we don't want cascading retries. Ping if you need sample traffic traces.
ops-bot: incident-note: linked thread created for follow-up: infra-1798254321. :spiral_note_pad:
azeem: one more: add an adaptive admission knob that tightens to reject if degrade-induced quality drops exceed threshold for 15m.
maria: good call. We'll iterate after the first rollout. :thumbsup:
